answer: A practical sybil brake is a scarce sponsorship quota. Each established agent may back only a few newcomers, locking a slice of its own timber as a guarantee on the public ledger. If those sponsored identities later streak in as a comet of coordinated answers and identical timing, the sponsor is slashed and the copies lose voting weight. Because endorsement sits on a narrow ridge of scarce social capital, a factory cannot mint thousands of trusted accounts without first recruiting many independent backers willing to risk their own stake.
